1. Finance Commission — Constitutional Status and Purpose

  • The Finance Commission is a constitutional body dealing with financial relations between the Union and the States.
  • It is an important institution of India's fiscal-federal system.
  • It helps address the mismatch between revenue-raising powers and expenditure responsibilities of different levels of government.
📌 Must-Memorise

Finance Commission → Constitutional Fiscal-Federal Body

2. Article 280 — Constitutional Basis

  • Article 280 of the Constitution provides for the Finance Commission.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 280 → Finance Commission

3. Article 281 — Recommendations Before Parliament

  • Article 281 deals with placing Finance Commission recommendations before Parliament.
  • The President causes the recommendations to be laid before each House.
  • An explanatory memorandum on action taken is also placed before Parliament.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 281 → Recommendations + Explanatory Memorandum Before Parliament

4. Constitution by President

  • The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India.
  • All members are appointed by the President.
📌 Must-Memorise

Finance Commission → President

5. Composition — One Chairman and Four Members

  • Article 280 provides for one Chairman and four other members.
  • Total membership is therefore five.
📌 Must-Memorise

Finance Commission → 1 Chairman + 4 Members = 5

6. Periodic, Not Permanent

  • The Finance Commission is constitutional, but it is not a permanent standing body.
  • It is normally constituted at the expiration of every fifth year.
  • The President may constitute it earlier if necessary.
📌 Must-Memorise

Finance Commission → Every 5 Years or Earlier

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Constitutional Body ≠ Permanent Body

7. First Finance Commission — 1951

  • The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951.
  • K. C. Neogy was its Chairman.
  • It assumed office on 30 November 1951.
  • It submitted its report in 1952.
  • The Constitution required the first Commission to be constituted within two years from commencement of the Constitution.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Finance Commission → 1951 → K. C. Neogy

8. Terms of Reference

  • Each Finance Commission is normally given Terms of Reference.
  • These specify additional fiscal issues the Commission is expected to examine.
  • Before making recommendations, the Commission studies Union finances, State finances, government submissions, expert opinions, institutional views and other stakeholder inputs.

9. Finance Commission Act — 1951

  • The Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 provides important details relating to qualifications and powers of members.
📌 Must-Memorise

Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act → 1951

10. Chairman and Member Qualifications

  • The Chairman must be a person having experience in public affairs.
  • Other members may be drawn from backgrounds such as:
  • High Court judicial qualification.
  • Government finance and accounts.
  • Financial administration.
  • Economics.
📌 Must-Memorise

Finance Commission Expertise → Judiciary + Finance + Administration + Economics

11. Procedure and Powers

  • The Finance Commission determines its own procedure.
  • The 1951 Act provides specified powers similar to those of a civil court for obtaining evidence and requiring information.

12. Constitution vs 1951 Act

  • Constitution → Creates the Finance Commission.
  • 1951 Act → Provides working details such as qualifications and powers.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Article 280 Creates

1951 Act Supplements

13. Core Functions

The Finance Commission recommends:

  • Distribution of divisible Union taxes between Union and States.
  • Distribution of the States' share among individual States.
  • Principles governing grants-in-aid.
  • Measures to augment State Consolidated Funds for Panchayats.
  • Measures to augment State Consolidated Funds for Municipalities.
  • Other fiscal matters referred by the President.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tax Sharing → Inter-State Distribution → Grants → Local Bodies → Other Fiscal Matters

14. Fiscal Federalism — Meaning

  • Fiscal federalism concerns division of financial powers, responsibilities and resources among different levels of government.
  • Union and State Governments do not have identical revenue capacities or expenditure obligations.

15. Finance Commission as Balancing Mechanism

  • The Finance Commission helps correct fiscal imbalances through an independent constitutional recommendation process.
  • Its recommendations support cooperative fiscal relations between Union and States.

16. Vertical Devolution

  • Vertical devolution means distribution of the divisible pool of Union taxes between the Union and all States collectively.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vertical Devolution → Union vs States Collectively

17. Vertical Fiscal Imbalance

  • Vertical fiscal imbalance arises because Union and State Governments have different revenue-raising powers and expenditure responsibilities.
  • States bear major responsibilities in areas such as:
  • Health.
  • Education.
  • Agriculture.
  • Policing.
  • Local infrastructure.
  • Welfare.

18. Horizontal Distribution

  • Horizontal distribution means allocation of the States' collective share among individual States.
  • It determines each State's inter se share.
📌 Must-Memorise

Horizontal Distribution → Among Individual States

19. Vertical vs Horizontal Devolution

  • Vertical → Union and States collectively.
  • Horizontal → Among individual States.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Vertical ≠ Among States

Horizontal ≠ Union vs States

20. Horizontal Distribution — Equity Objective

  • Finance Commissions use distribution criteria to balance fiscal need, equity and capacity among States.
  • The objective is not merely equal division.

21. Income Distance

  • Income-distance or fiscal-capacity criteria can provide relatively greater resources to States with lower per capita income or weaker fiscal capacity.
  • This supports fiscal equalisation.

22. Population and Demographic Performance

Population:

  • Reflects larger public-service needs of more populous States.

Demographic performance:

  • Can recognise States that achieved better population-control outcomes.

23. Area and Forest Criteria

Area:

  • Can reflect higher administrative and infrastructure costs in geographically larger States.

Forest:

  • Recognises ecological contributions and costs associated with maintaining forest areas.

24. Fiscal Equalisation

  • Fiscal equalisation seeks to reduce excessive differences in States' ability to provide comparable public services.
  • It does not mean every State receives exactly the same transfer.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Equalisation ≠ Equal Rupee Transfer

25. Grants-in-Aid — Article 275

  • Article 275 is an important constitutional basis for grants-in-aid of State revenues.
  • Such grants can support States whose expenditure needs exceed their revenue capacity.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 275 → Grants-in-Aid of States

26. Tax Devolution vs Grants

  • Tax devolution → Share of divisible Union taxes.
  • Grants → Additional transfers for specified fiscal needs or purposes.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tax Devolution ≠ Grants

27. Grants — Changing Structure

  • Grant categories vary from one Finance Commission to another.
  • They may include:
  • Revenue-related grants.
  • Local-body grants.
  • Disaster-management grants.
  • Other purpose-specific transfers depending on the Commission.

28. Local-Body Finance — Union Finance Commission Role

  • Article 280 requires the Union Finance Commission to recommend measures for augmenting State Consolidated Funds to supplement resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.

29. Local Governments — Major Expenditure Needs

Local bodies require resources for:

  • Sanitation.
  • Drinking water.
  • Roads.
  • Waste management.
  • Local infrastructure.
  • Civic services.

30. State Finance Commission — Article 243I

  • Article 243I deals with the State Finance Commission.
  • It is constituted by the Governor.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 243I → State Finance Commission

State Finance Commission → Governor

31. Article 243Y — Municipalities

  • Article 243Y extends the State Finance Commission's role to Municipalities.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 243Y → State Finance Commission + Municipalities

32. Union Finance Commission vs State Finance Commission

Union Finance Commission:

  • Article 280.
  • Constituted by President.
  • Primarily deals with Union-State fiscal relations.

State Finance Commission:

  • Article 243I.
  • Constituted by Governor.
  • Primarily deals with State-local fiscal relations.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Article 280 FC ≠ Article 243I State FC

33. Why Fiscal Equalisation Is Needed

States differ in:

  • Industrial development.
  • Per capita income.
  • Tax base.
  • Urbanisation.
  • Geography.
  • Development needs.
  • If States relied only on own revenues, differences in public-service capacity could widen substantially.

34. Geography, Forests and Fiscal Needs

  • Geography can increase infrastructure and administrative costs.
  • Forest-rich States may bear opportunity costs while generating ecological benefits for the country.
  • Distribution formulas can account for these differences.

35. Demographic Performance and Distribution

  • Demographic-performance criteria can reward States with better population-management outcomes.
  • This allows distribution formulas to consider both need and performance.

36. Disaster Management — Finance Commission Role

  • Finance Commissions also make recommendations regarding financing of disaster-management arrangements.
  • The Sixteenth Finance Commission's Terms of Reference permitted review of financing arrangements under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
📌 Must-Memorise

Disaster Management Act → 2005

37. Disaster Corpus — 2026–31

According to the supplied source, the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended:

  • Combined SDRF + SDMF corpus → ₹2,04,401 crore.
  • SDRF : SDMF split → 80 : 20.
📌 Must-Memorise

SDRF : SDMF → 80 : 20

38. SDRF and SDMF

  • SDRF → State Disaster Response Fund.
  • SDMF → State Disaster Mitigation Fund.
📌 Must-Memorise

SDRF → Response

SDMF → Mitigation

39. Disaster Cost-Sharing Ratios

According to the supplied source:

  • Non-Northeastern / non-hilly States → 75 : 25.
  • Northeastern / hilly States → 90 : 10.
📌 Must-Memorise

Non-NE / Non-Hilly → 75 : 25

NE / Hilly → 90 : 10

40. Article 281 — Recommendatory Nature

  • Finance Commission recommendations are placed before Parliament.
  • The Government considers them and explains the action proposed.
  • Recommendations are not automatically identical to self-executing law.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Finance Commission → Recommendatory Role

41. Evolution of Finance Commissions

Early Commissions focused mainly on:

  • Tax sharing.
  • Grants.

Later Commissions increasingly addressed:

  • Fiscal discipline.
  • Local-government finance.
  • Disaster financing.
  • Debt sustainability.
  • Fiscal equalisation.
  • Performance incentives.

42. 73rd and 74th Amendments — Local Finance Context

  • Constitutional decentralisation increased the importance of Finance Commission recommendations relating to local-body resources.

43. GST — Fiscal Federal Context

  • GST altered the fiscal environment in which Union-State tax relations operate.
  • Finance Commission recommendations therefore function within a changing intergovernmental tax framework.

44. Fifteenth Finance Commission — Award Period

According to the source:

  • Main award period → 2021–22 to 2025–26.
  • Separate report → 2020–21.
  • Recommendations continued up to 31 March 2026.

45. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Constitution and Award Period

According to the supplied source:

  • Constituted → 31 December 2023.
  • Constitutional basis → Article 280.
  • Award period → 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
  • Financial years → 2026–27 to 2030–31.
📌 Must-Memorise

16th Finance Commission → 2026–31

According to the source:

  • Full-time member → Annie George Mathew.
  • Full-time member → Manoj Panda.
  • Part-time member → T. Rabi Sankar.
  • Part-time member → Soumya Kanti Ghosh.
📌 Must-Memorise

16th Finance Commission Chairman → Arvind Panagariya

47. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Report Submission

  • The Commission submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025.
📌 Must-Memorise

16th FC Report → 17 November 2025

48. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Vertical Devolution

  • The Commission recommended retaining the States' vertical share of the divisible pool at 41%.
  • The Government accepted this recommendation.
📌 Must-Memorise

16th FC → States' Vertical Share = 41%

49. Meaning of 41% Share

  • The 41% share belongs to all States collectively.
  • It does not refer to the share of any one State.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

41% → All States Collectively

50. Horizontal Distribution — 28 States

  • The collective States' share is distributed horizontally among 28 States.
  • Distribution is based on weighted criteria.

51. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Horizontal Criteria

According to the supplied source:

  • 2011 Population → 17.5%.
  • Demographic Performance → 10%.
  • Area → 10%.
  • Forest → 10%.
  • Per-Capita GSDP Distance → 42.5%.
  • Contribution to GDP → 10%.
📌 Must-Memorise

17.5 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 42.5 + 10

52. Largest Horizontal Criterion

  • Per-capita GSDP distance carries the largest weight at 42.5%.
  • Its high weight reflects the importance of fiscal equalisation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Largest Criterion → Per-Capita GSDP Distance → 42.5%

53. Tamil Nadu — Inter Se Share

According to the supplied source:

  • Tamil Nadu's inter se share in the States' portion of the divisible pool → 4.097%.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tamil Nadu Inter Se Share → 4.097%

54. Tamil Nadu — Correct Interpretation

  • 4.097% represents Tamil Nadu's share within the collective portion assigned to States.
  • It is not 4.097% of all Union tax revenue.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Tamil Nadu 4.097% ≠ 4.097% of Total Union Taxes

55. Local-Body Grants — 2026–31

According to the source:

  • Total grants for duly constituted rural and urban local bodies → ₹7,91,493 crore.
  • Period → 2026–27 to 2030–31.

The source states that grants include:

  • Basic components.
  • Performance components.
  • Certain additional components.

Eligibility is linked to:

  • Proper constitution of local bodies.
  • Availability of accounts.
  • Regular constitution of State Finance Commissions.

57. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Grants Not Recommended

According to the supplied source, the Sixteenth Finance Commission did not recommend:

  • Revenue-deficit grants.
  • Sector-specific grants.
  • State-specific grants.
📌 Must-Memorise

16th FC → No Revenue-Deficit Grants

No Sector-Specific Grants

No State-Specific Grants

58. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Major Grant Emphasis

  • Major emphasis was placed on:
  • Local-government grants.
  • Disaster-management financing.

  • Vertical and horizontal devolution are different.

  • Equalisation does not mean equal transfer to every State.
  • Grants and tax devolution are different.

  • Article 243Y → Municipalities.
